settings.text: Plenty of dogs claim a new bed the first evening. Some take a fortnight. Both are normal, and you've got [nights].

settings.title: Not right? Tell us
settings.text: Any time inside the [nights] nights. We collect it free from the UK mainland and refund every penny.

settings.question: How do I measure my dog?
settings.answer: Wait until they're asleep and stretched out. Measure from the nose to the base of the tail, then add about 20cm. Between sizes, or a puppy still growing? Go up one: a bed a little too big is fine, one too small isn't.

settings.question: Why does it ask about their joints?
settings.answer: Because that decides what the bed needs to be made of. A young, bouncy dog can sleep on anything soft. A dog who pauses at the bottom of the stairs needs a core that spreads their weight and a front that's easy to step over.

settings.question: What if the result isn't right?
settings.answer: Change an answer and it picks again. And whatever you choose, you've got [nights] nights at home to be sure, with free collection if it isn't right.

settings.heading: How the finder decides.
settings.lede: It reads each bed's own data: what's inside, how it's shaped, which dogs each size lists. It never guesses, and it never recommends a bed that's sold out in your size.
